question: What kind of ill-situated liṅga is distinguished by lacking faults but lacking worship?
premises: A liṅga may be free from decay and other faults.
The same liṅga may be devoid of worship.
Such a liṅga may still be ill-situated.
inference: Therefore, an ill-situated liṅga can be physically sound yet neglected in worship.
plain_english: But an ill-situated liṅga may be free from decay and other faults, yet devoid of worship.
